Bhojpur: Home of the Bhojpure khukuri, forged in the Rai hills above the Arun valley.
Dhankuta: Orange and tea hills around the former Eastern Region headquarters.
Ilam: Nepal's tea capital — orthodox tea gardens have grown here since 1863.
Jhapa: Nepal's easternmost district and its lowest-lying land, on the fertile Mechi plain.
Khotang: Halesi Mahadev, called the 'Pashupatinath of the East,' sacred to Hindus, Buddhists and Kirats.
Morang: Nepal's third most populous district, anchored by industrial Biratnagar.
Okhaldhunga: Quiet eastern hills that raised Siddhicharan Shrestha, Nepal's 'poet of the era.'
Panchthar: The Limbu heartland of eastern Nepal, centred on the hill bazaar of Phidim.
Sankhuwasabha: Makalu's district — from the Arun gorge to the world's fifth-highest peak.
Solukhumbu: Everest's district — Sagarmatha National Park and the Sherpa Khumbu region.
Sunsari: Dharan, Itahari and the Koshi Tappu wetlands sit at eastern Nepal's crossroads.
Taplejung: Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, and the Pathibhara pilgrimage site.
Terhathum: Gateway to Tinjure–Milke–Jaljale, the 'rhododendron capital of Nepal.'
Udayapur: Inner-Tarai valley district home to the state-owned Udayapur Cement factory.
Bara: Home to Gadhimai's quinquennial festival and the medieval capital Simraungadh.
Dhanusha: Janakpurdham, Madhesh's capital — the Janaki Mandir and Nepal's only operating railway.
Mahottari: Jaleshwar's 'God in water' Shiva temple, and Bardibas where two major highways meet.
Parsa: Birgunj, Nepal's main trade gateway to India, plus the tiger forests of Parsa National Park.
Rautahat: A Bajjika-speaking heartland with more municipalities (16) than any other Nepali district.
Saptari: Home to the Koshi Barrage and Koshi Tappu's wild water buffalo.
Sarlahi: Holds Nepal's record 20 local levels, plus the Lalbandi vegetable belt.
Siraha: Home to Salhesh Fulbari and Lahan's well-known Sagarmatha Eye Hospital.
Bhaktapur: The medieval Newar city of Bhaktapur Durbar Square — Nepal's smallest and fastest-growing district.
Chitawan: Chitwan National Park, one-horned rhinos, and the metropolitan city of Bharatpur.
Dhading: Ganesh Himal country, immediately west of Kathmandu, split by the Prithvi Highway.
Dolakha: Home to the Kalinchok shrine and Nepal's largest hydropower plant, Upper Tamakoshi.
Kathmandu: Nepal's capital district — the most populous, densest and most literate in the country.
Kabhrepalanchok: Dhulikhel, Banepa and Panauti — historic Newar towns on the old Kathmandu–Tibet trade road.
Lalitpur: Patan Durbar Square and the Newar fine-arts city of Lalitpur.
Makawanpur: Hetauda, Bagmati Province's capital, sits beneath the Daman viewpoint.
Nuwakot: The seven-storey Nuwakot Durbar — the fortress-palace where Nepal's unification campaign began.
Ramechhap: Home to Manthali Airport, a busy seasonal gateway for Lukla–Everest flights.
Rasuwa: The Langtang valley, the sacred Gosainkunda lakes, and the Rasuwagadhi crossing to China.
Sindhuli: Home to Sindhuli Gadhi, where Gorkhali forces routed a British East India Company expedition in 1767.
Sindhupalchok: Bhote Koshi gorge country on the old China road — hit hardest by the 2015 earthquake.
Baglung: Nepal's 'district of suspension bridges' above the Kali Gandaki river.
Gorkha: Cradle of Nepal's unification, Prithvi Narayan Shah's Gorkha Durbar, and home of Manaslu (8,163 m).
Kaski: Home of Pokhara, Nepal's tourism capital, beneath Machhapuchhre and the Annapurnas.
Lamjung: Besisahar, trailhead of the Annapurna Circuit, and Nepal's densest Gurung heartland.
Manang: Nepal's least populous district — the trans-Himalayan upper Marsyangdi valley.
Mustang: The walled city of Lo Manthang, Muktinath, and the world's deepest gorge nearby.
Myagdi: Dhaulagiri I (8,167 m), the Poon Hill viewpoint, and the hot springs of Tatopani.
Nawalparasi East: Gandaki Province's only Tarai district, anchored by Kawasoti on the Narayani plain.
Parbat: Home to Kushma's canyon-spanning suspension bridges and a famous high bungee jump.
Syangja: Nepal's leading orange-growing district, home to the 144 MW Kaligandaki A power station.
Tanahu: Birthplace of Adikavi Bhanubhakta Acharya, and home to the hilltop town of Bandipur.
Arghakhanchi: Home to the wish-granting Supa Deurali shrine in Nepal's western hills.
Banke: Nepalgunj, the gateway city of the western Tarai, and Banke National Park.
Bardiya: Bardiya National Park — the Tarai's largest, a tiger and wild-elephant stronghold.
Dang: The Dang and Deukhuri valleys — Tharu heartland and seat of Lumbini Province's capital.
Gulmi: Birthplace of Nepali coffee, beneath the sacred Resunga hill.
Kapilbastu: Home to Tilaurakot, the walled remains of ancient Kapilavastu.
Nawalparasi West: Home to the Ramgram stupa — the only one of the Buddha's original relic stupas never opened.
Palpa: The hill bazaar of Tansen, known for Palpali dhaka weaving and Sen-era history.
Pyuthan: Home to Swargadwari, the hilltop 'gateway to heaven.'
Rolpa: Cradle of the 1996–2006 Maoist insurgency, now the Magar highlands of the Guerrilla Trek.
Rukum East: Kham Magar high country beneath Putha Hiunchuli, with most of the Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve.
Rupandehi: Home to Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, and the booming Butwal–Bhairahawa corridor.
Dailekh: Home to Dullu's medieval Khasa-empire inscriptions and the Panchakoshi pilgrimage.
Dolpa: Nepal's largest district — trans-Himalayan Dolpo, Shey Phoksundo National Park and its lake.
Humla: Nepal's remotest district — the Limi Valley and the Hilsa gateway to Mount Kailash.
Jajarkot: A Bheri-basin hill district, epicentre of Nepal's deadly November 2023 earthquake.
Jumla: Known for organic apples and the Sinja Valley, cradle of the Nepali language.
Kalikot: A rugged mid-Karnali district where the steep Karnali Highway clings to the gorge.
Mugu: Home to Rara, Nepal's largest lake, in one of the country's remotest districts.
Rukum West: The Karnali half of old Rukum — a cradle district of the Maoist 'People's War.'
Salyan: Karnali's southern hill district and one of Nepal's leading ginger producers.
Surkhet: Karnali Province's capital, Birendranagar, and the 12th-century Kakrebihar temple.
Achham: Home to Ramaroshan's lakes and meadows on the southern flanks of Khaptad.
Baitadi: Home to the Tripurasundari temple and birthplace of martyr Dashrath Chand.
Bajhang: Home to Saipal Himal (7,031 m) and reformer-raja Jaya Prithvi Bahadur Singh.
Bajura: Home to the Badimalika temple pilgrimage in Nepal's remote far-western high country.
Dadeldhura: Home to Amargadhi Fort, once Amar Singh Thapa's western stronghold.
Darchula: Home to Api Himal (7,132 m) on the Mahakali frontier with India.
Doti: Seat of the medieval Doti Kingdom and the Shaileshwari temple.
Kailali: Home to Dhangadhi, Ghodaghodi Lake, and Nepal's only cable-stayed bridge.
Kanchanpur: Home to Shuklaphanta National Park and some of the world's largest swamp deer herds.
